title: Russia sanctions bill advances in US House, set for final vote
summary: The US House of Representatives advanced the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which authorizes tariffs on nations trading oil and gas with Russia.

headlines.title: Will India resist US tariff pressure amid trade deal? Trump plans to sign Russia sanctions bill

lens_briefs.reader: The US House of Representatives has passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, authorizing the president to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying significant volumes of Russian oil and gas, with an amendment explicitly naming India and other major buyers. What began as a sanctions push against Moscow's energy trade now threatens steep US duties on goods from India and China, the largest buyers of discounted Russian crude. Indian business coverage, ranging from neutral reporting to alarmist takes, frames the bill as a serious trade risk for India. Delhi has responded by saying it will protect its economic interests, Beijing rejects the measure as unilateral long-arm jurisdiction, and the Kremlin has criticized the bill. Whether the Senate passes it and how the president applies the tariff authority remain unresolved. Watch Indian and Chinese crude-buying patterns and any signs of trade retaliation.

perspectives.label: US Congress / bill sponsors (Graham Act proponents)
perspectives.stance: Sanction Russia's energy trade via presidential authority to impose up to 100% tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil and gas
perspectives.summary: Coverage relayed mostly by neutral Indian business press describes the House passing the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, granting the president power to levy tariffs of up to 100% on significant importers of Russian oil and gas. An amendment explicitly names India and other trading partners as targets, framing India and China as the most exposed buyers.

perspectives.label: Indian government / Indian trade stakeholders
perspectives.stance: Opposes the tariff threat, asserts it will protect India's economic interests
perspectives.summary: Delhi responded to the bill's passage by stating its determination to protect India's economic interests. Critical and alarmist Indian coverage emphasizes that the law could bring significant or 100% tariffs on Indian goods over Russian oil purchases, framing it as a material trade risk to the economy.

perspectives.label: China (Beijing)
perspectives.stance: Rejects the US tariff plan as unlawful extraterritorial overreach
perspectives.summary: Beijing rejects US plans to tariff countries purchasing Russian energy, citing opposition to unilateral long-arm jurisdiction — casting the law as coercive extraterritorial regulation rather than legitimate sanctions.

perspectives.label: Kremlin (Russian government)
perspectives.stance: Criticizes the bill as hostile US escalation
perspectives.summary: The Kremlin criticized the House passage of the sanctions bill, while Indian reporting alongside it raised concerns over energy-import exposure for countries like India buying Russian crude.
